conditions.label: Venous air embolism
conditions.note: After right internal jugular central line placed with patient upright.

reports.text: Portable AP chest, single view, after right internal jugular central venous catheter placement. Catheter enters from the right neck with its tip projecting over the lower superior vena cava. No pneumothorax. Lungs clear without consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal for technique. Mediastinal contour normal. No acute osseous abnormality of the visualized chest.
reports.conclusion: Right internal jugular catheter in satisfactory position. No acute cardiopulmonary findings.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate about 130. Normal axis. Intervals within normal limits. Nonspecific ST-T wave changes. No prior tracing available for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST-T changes.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Trauma center emergency department, physician record. Date of service 2026-06-20. Received by fax 2026-07-09.

HPI: 41-year-old man arriving by ambulance after a high-speed motor vehicle collision. Trauma activation. On arrival he is tachycardic and hypotensive. History of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity and obstructive sleep apnea per patient and medication list.

Peripheral IV attempts unsuccessful, so a right internal jugular central venous catheter was placed emergently while he was sitting up. Within minutes of placement he became acutely short of breath, described a vague tightness in the chest and felt dizzy. His pressure fell further and he began gasping.

Exam after the change: neck veins distended. Mildly confused, follows commands. A new systolic murmur, loudest along the left sternal border. Lungs clear on both sides.

Studies: portable chest film shows the line well placed and nothing else acute. Bedside cardiac ultrasound attempted, windows too poor to interpret. ECG sinus tachycardia, nonspecific ST-T changes.

Impression: venous air embolism associated with central line placement in the upright position; multiple traumatic injuries.

ED course: catheter hub occluded. Patient turned onto his left side with the head of the bed lowered. 100% oxygen by non-rebreather. Over the next hour pressure and breathing improved and his mentation cleared. Orthopedic surgery consulted for his injuries.

Home medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, about 8 pack-years, quit two years ago. Alcohol socially. Construction site supervisor.

Disposition: admitted to orthopedic surgery for operative fixation.

documents.title: Outside records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ED packet from the trauma center received: physician record, chest film report, ECG. No admission or operative notes in the packet. Routed to PCP.

events.reason: Multiple orthopedic injuries after motor vehicle collision

documents.title: Orthopedic Surgery Inpatient Progress Note
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopedic surgery inpatient progress note, hospital day 10 (2026-06-30). Received 2026-08-14.

Interval: 41-year-old man admitted after a motor vehicle collision, course complicated in the ED by air embolism after central line placement. Now status post open reduction and internal fixation of multiple orthopedic injuries. Anticipate several more weeks of restricted mobility.

New today: flaccid paralysis of the legs. Nursing and nutrition note a marked loss of lean body mass, worst in the lower limbs, although he has been meeting his nutrition goals.

Exam: awake, alert, oriented to person, place and time. Afebrile. Visible muscle wasting of both lower extremities with reduced strength. Incisions clean and dry. No signs of systemic infection.

Medications: enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous daily for clot prophylaxis; home lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin; metformin held while inpatient, glucose managed per protocol.
Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: continue physical therapy, nutrition support, physiatry consultation for rehabilitation placement. Continue DVT prophylaxis.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was in a bad car wreck Saturday. Im at the trauma hospital, they did surgery on a bunch of broken stuff. Something went wrong with the IV in my neck in the ER too. I wont make the appointment tomorrow obviously. Will let you know when I get out

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, I'm so sorry, and glad you reached out. Focus on getting better. We'll cancel tomorrow and request the hospital records so I'm up to speed. Message or call when you're discharged and we'll get you in.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed request to the trauma center health information office for ED record, operative notes, imaging and discharge summary when available. Patient release on file. Told 7-10 business days.

documents.title: Enoxaparin prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Retail pharmacy called: enoxaparin 40 mg daily syringes written at his discharge from an inpatient rehab facility on 7/24 need a prior auth, and the rehab prescriber's office is not answering. Pharmacy fill history also shows acetaminophen-oxycodone 5/325 #20 filled 7/24. First we have heard he was in rehab. PCP reviewed: completed PA with the insurer by phone citing post-operative orthopedic trauma and immobility, approved through 8/7. Pharmacy notified. Neither drug added to our prescriptions; recorded as outside meds.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after hearing from the pharmacy. Discharged from the hospital to inpatient rehab on 7/6, home since Friday 7/24. Getting around the apartment with a rolling walker, home exercises from rehab. Legs still weak. Doing the daily enoxaparin shots himself, finishes 8/7. Uses the pain pills mostly at night. Back on metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin. Using CPAP. No fever, chest pain, breathing trouble or calf swelling. A neighbor is helping with groceries. Booked with PCP Wed 8/5. Asked him to bring any discharge papers.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, his ride fell through and he can't drive yet. Offered video, he would rather be seen in person. Rebooked 8/19 at 10:00; reminded him of the medical transport benefit on his plan.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since the crash on 6/20. Came by medical transport, walking in with a rolling walker.

What we know: ED record (received 7/9) describes a venous air embolism right after an emergency right IJ line was placed with him sitting up; treated with positioning and high-flow oxygen, recovered. Admitted to orthopedics for ORIF of multiple injuries. Orthopedic day-10 note (received 8/14) documents new flaccid paralysis of the legs with loss of lean mass in the lower limbs despite good nutrition; awake and oriented, no infection. Physiatry, then inpatient rehab 7/6 to 7/24. We still do not have the operative notes, discharge summary or rehab summary.

Since home: home exercises daily, legs a bit stronger each week. Can do short distances in the apartment with the walker, needs a rest after the parking lot. No falls. Pain mild, finished the oxycodone-acetaminophen early this month, uses nothing now. Enoxaparin finished 8/7 as directed. Back on his usual 4 meds since rehab. CPAP nightly. No chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations or confusion. Eating well. Out of work; employer has him on short-term disability. Mood "frustrated but okay." PHQ-2 1.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, aspirin 81 daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 124/78, weight 101.5 kg (110 in January). Alert, oriented, conversant. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Surgical incisions healed, no redness or drainage. Visible wasting of the thighs and calves on both sides. Strength: hip flexion 4-/5 R and L, knee extension 4-/5 R and L, ankle dorsiflexion 4/5 R and L. Light touch intact in both legs. Calves soft, nontender, no swelling. Gait slow with walker, steady.

A/P
1. Venous air embolism: resolved in the ED, no lasting symptoms; murmur not present today. Moved to resolved.
2. Flaccid paralysis of both legs after the trauma admission: improving. Outpatient PT referral placed to keep the rehab momentum; he wants a clinic close to home. Added to problem list.
3. Multiple orthopedic injuries s/p ORIF: following with orthopedics; healing incisions. Second records request today.
4. T2DM: weight down about 9 kg, much of it muscle. A1c, BMP, CBC today. Continue metformin.
5. HTN: lower today with the weight change; keep lisinopril 20, watch for dizziness on standing (none so far).
6. Statin and aspirin continued. OSA on CPAP.
7. Work: disability paperwork when it arrives.
Follow-up about 6 weeks, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Second records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second fax to the trauma center for operative notes and discharge summary, and first request to the inpatient rehabilitation facility for their discharge summary. Release signed today.

documents.body: Henry, A1c is 6.9, the best it has been. Blood counts and kidney function are normal. No changes. PT should be calling you this week to set up the first session.
